title: AutoGen
oneLiner: Multi-agent AI framework from Microsoft Research for building conversational agent systems with AgentChat, Core API, and Extensions.
summary: AutoGen is Microsoft Research's open-source framework for building multi-agent AI systems. It provides three layers — AgentChat for quick prototyping, Core API for fine-grained control, and Extensions for ecosystem integrations — giving developers a flexible foundation for agent collaboration patterns.
whyItMatters: AutoGen matters because it comes from one of the most well-resourced AI research labs in the world and is designed around the principle that agent conversations are the fundamental primitive for multi-agent systems. Its layered architecture lets developers start simple and add complexity as needed.
bestFor: Research teams studying agent collaboration patterns and emergent behavior
Engineers who need fine-grained control over agent state, messaging, and orchestration
notFor: Developers who only need a single-agent terminal coding tool
Teams looking for a drag-and-drop workflow builder with a visual UI

coreStrengths.title: Layered architecture
coreStrengths.description: AutoGen provides three layers: AgentChat for rapid prototyping, Core API for fine-grained control, and Extensions for ecosystem integrations.
coreStrengths.whyItMatters: Developers can start with the simplest layer and add complexity as their needs grow, without rewriting their codebase.

coreStrengths.title: Conversation-centric design
coreStrengths.description: Agent conversations are the fundamental primitive. Agents collaborate through structured message passing with built-in conversation patterns.
coreStrengths.whyItMatters: Conversation-centric design makes it natural to model complex multi-agent interactions like debates, reviews, and iterative refinement.

coreStrengths.title: Microsoft ecosystem integration
coreStrengths.description: Backed by Microsoft Research with deep integration into Azure AI services and the broader Microsoft developer ecosystem.
coreStrengths.whyItMatters: Teams already on Azure get first-class support, and the Microsoft backing means long-term maintenance and enterprise readiness.

seoArticle.intro: AutoGen is Microsoft Research's framework for building multi-agent AI systems. It treats agent conversations as the fundamental building block and provides a layered architecture that scales from quick prototypes to production systems.
seoArticle.whatItIs: AutoGen is an open-source framework for building conversational multi-agent systems. It offers three layers: AgentChat for rapid prototyping with pre-built conversation patterns, Core API for fine-grained control over agent state and messaging, and Extensions for integrating with external tools and services. Agents collaborate through structured message passing.
seoArticle.whyItMatters: Multi-agent systems are becoming the standard approach for complex AI tasks, but building them from scratch is hard. AutoGen provides the primitives — agent registration, message routing, conversation management, state handling — so developers can focus on designing agent behaviors rather than infrastructure.
seoArticle.howItWorks: Install via pip and choose your entry layer. AgentChat gives you pre-built conversation patterns for quick experiments. Core API gives you full control over agent lifecycle, messaging, and state. Extensions connect to external tools and services. Define your agents, set up their conversation patterns, and let AutoGen orchestrate the collaboration.

useCases.title: Multi-agent code generation
useCases.description: Build a pipeline where a planner agent designs the implementation, a coder agent writes it, and a reviewer agent checks it before committing.

useCases.title: Research synthesis
useCases.description: Create agents that specialize in different aspects of a research question and synthesize their findings into a coherent analysis.

useCases.title: Customer support orchestration
useCases.description: Route customer queries through a triage agent to specialized support agents, with escalation patterns for complex issues.

alternatives.title: Use CrewAI for a more accessible API
alternatives.summary: AutoGen offers more control and flexibility. CrewAI has a gentler learning curve and more intuitive role-based design.

alternatives.title: Use a single agent for simple tasks
alternatives.summary: If your task doesn't require multiple specialized agents, a single-agent tool like Claude Code or Aider will be simpler and faster.

faq.question: Is AutoGen open source?
faq.answer: Yes. AutoGen is released under the CC-BY-4.0 license, making the source code available for inspection, modification, and redistribution.

faq.question: Who should use AutoGen?
faq.answer: Developers building conversational multi-agent systems, especially those who need fine-grained control over agent state, messaging, and orchestration patterns.

faq.question: How does AutoGen compare to other multi-agent frameworks?
faq.answer: AutoGen's main advantage is its layered architecture and conversation-centric design. It offers more low-level control than CrewAI but has a steeper learning curve.
